title: Gallipoli campaign
summary: On 19 February 1915 British and French ships began a naval assault on the Dardanelles, meant to open the way to Constantinople. Military landings on the Gallipoli peninsula followed on 25 April, and by mid-January 1916 all Allied troops had been evacuated. IWM puts total campaign casualties at more than half a million, and the Australian War Memorial records 26,111 Australian casualties including 8,141 deaths.

uncertainty.note: Start is the naval assault of 19 February 1915; end is the evacuation of the last Allied troops (9 January 1916 per IWM; the Australian War Memorial gives 19–20 December 1915 for the Australian evacuation).

as_recorded.value: On 19 February 1915, British and French ships began a naval assault on the Dardanelles
On the 9th of January 1916, the last remaining Allied troops on the Gallipoli peninsula were evacuated

where.historical_name: Gallipoli peninsula and the Dardanelles, Ottoman Empire

importance.justification: IWM calls the Dardanelles campaign one of the First World War’s most controversial episodes, with more than half a million casualties.

sources.title: A Short History Of The World War 1 Dardanelles Campaign

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date: IWM gives 9 January 1916 and 'mid-January 1916' on the same page, while the Australian War Memorial gives 19–20 December for the evacuation of the Australians; the record uses IWM. The pin is the peninsula (GeoNames), though the 19 February action was at the Dardanelles forts at its tip. Only IWM and AWM casualty figures were opened, so no per-nation Ottoman or Allied totals are given.
